packages.title: DESNZ activity versus spend method guard
facts: 2026 factors calculate emissions from activity data.
Fuel volume is supported activity data.
Purchased electricity kWh is supported activity data.
Travel distance is supported activity data.
Scope 1 can be reported separately.
Scope 2 can be reported separately.
Scope 3 can be reported separately.
The factor set is updated annually.
Activity factors differ from Defra spend multipliers.
A factor alone is not a parcel measurement.

packages.title: DESNZ factor quality governance
facts: 2026 factors have a Code compliance statement.
Trustworthiness is a Code pillar.
Quality is a Code pillar.
Value is a Code pillar.
Factors are a calculation tool, not statistics themselves.
They support activity-data emissions calculation.
They support SECR use cases.
Production sits with the DESNZ GHGI team.
Aether works under the NAEI contract.
Quality governance does not create site measurements.

packages.title: EA landfill methane measurement boundary
facts: EA published landfill methane research in February 2026.
The study assessed methane measurement methods.
It considered regulatory use of measurements.
Two measurement methods were investigated.
Measurements can test gas-management effectiveness.
Measurement may improve landfill-gas capture.
Methane forms as organic waste decomposes.
Landfills are an anthropogenic methane source.
Residual methane can be diffuse across a wide area.
Site measurements cannot be exported to unrelated parcels.

packages.title: DESNZ local waste and landfill category
facts: The local GHG report has a waste methodology section.
Waste process emissions are included in the local series.
The current series reaches back to 2005.
Waste electricity is handled under non-domestic electricity.
Energy-from-waste electricity follows end-user allocation.
Solid waste disposal is a key methane category.
Local waste values use spatial-disaggregation methods.
Local estimates are not plume measurements.
End-user and physical-source accounting can differ.
Parcel attribution needs geometry and source binding.

packages.title: Defra 2024 agriculture GHG shares
facts: Agriculture is around 13% of UK GHG emissions.
Agriculture emits nitrous oxide.
Agriculture emits methane.
Agriculture emits carbon dioxide.
Agriculture was 59% of UK N2O in 2024.
Agriculture was 49% of UK methane in 2024.
Agriculture was 2.5% of UK CO2 in 2024.
Agriculture was 89% of UK ammonia in 2024.
Agricultural emissions fell 15% from 1990 to 2024.
National shares are not parcel measurements.

packages.title: Defra agriculture N2O and methane trend
facts: Agriculture is a major N2O source.
Agriculture is a major methane source.
Its N2O share exceeds its CO2 share.
Its methane share exceeds its CO2 share.
Total N2O was lower in 2024 than 1990.
Non-agricultural reductions affect sector shares.
GHG values are part of the national inventory.
Inventory values are revised annually.
Gas identities must remain separate.
Parcel estimates need field-level activity evidence.

packages.title: ONS atmospheric-emissions gas coverage
facts: ONS publishes emissions by industry and gas.
The dataset includes CO2.
The dataset includes methane.
The dataset includes N2O.
The dataset includes HFCs.
The dataset includes PFCs.
The dataset includes SF6.
The dataset includes NF3.
The dataset includes total GHG emissions.
The series covers 1990-2024 and about 130 SIC groups.

packages.title: ONS current/provisional revision guard
facts: ONS provides current and provisional editions.
Current data cover all economic sectors.
Provisional data provide top-level estimates.
Previous dataset versions remain available.
Initial estimates can later be revised.
Method changes can trigger revisions.
System changes can trigger revisions.
Planned revisions differ from errors.
Errors are corrected and explained.
Current and provisional editions must not be silently mixed.

packages.title: EPC estimated-CO2 guard
facts: Domestic EPCs include an Energy Efficiency Rating.
EER is based on estimated fuel costs.
Domestic EPCs include an Environmental Impact Rating.
EIR is based on CO2 emissions.
Both ratings are estimated from property characteristics.
Ratings are banded A to G.
Higher ratings generally imply lower CO2.
EPCs are lodged on the building register.
EIR is not a continuous emissions measurement.
Building-to-parcel binding is required for parcel use.

packages.title: EPC local-authority revision guard
facts: Q1 2026 EPC statistics were revised on 19 May 2026.
A lookup-table processing error caused the revision.
The lookup assigned local authorities from postcodes.
The error increased unknown local authorities.
Some England/Wales allocations were wrong before revision.
The total impact was small relative to the dataset.
Subregional figures were the main affected outputs.
National headline figures were not materially changed.
Revised data are identified by MHCLG.
Downstream provenance should preserve the correction notice.

packages.title: New-dwelling EPC rating QA
facts: England logged 416,000 domestic EPCs in Q1 2026.
48,000 were for new dwellings.
New-dwelling lodgements rose year on year.
New dwellings usually had high ratings.
87% of new dwellings were rated A or B.
Band B was the most common new-dwelling EER.
EPC statistics use lodged certificates.
They are not a census of every building.
A high EPC rating is not measured operational GHG.
Parcel use needs certificate-to-building geometry matching.

packages.title: Non-domestic EPC rating QA
facts: Retail units and offices are non-domestic properties.
England logged 21,000 non-domestic EPCs in Q1 2026.
This count was lower year on year.
Non-domestic EPCs include an A+ band.
43% received A+, A or B.
Statistics are based on certificate lodgements.
Lodgements are not the total building stock.
Asset ratings are not direct emissions measurements.
They can support building-efficiency screening.
Parcel use needs explicit property identity matching.

packages.title: ONS weekly EPC dataset QA
facts: ONS publishes a weekly EPC dataset.
The retrieved latest edition is 16 July 2026.
It reports weekly new-property EPC counts.
It reports weekly existing-property EPC counts.
Coverage is England and Wales.
The source is MHCLG.
ONS labels it official statistics in development.
Multiple dated editions are retained.
Weekly counts are not parcel emissions.
Edition dates must be preserved in comparisons.

packages.title: EPC live-table CO2 fields QA
facts: Live EPC tables contain certificates since 2008.

They include energy-use information.
They include CO2-emissions information.
They include fuel-cost information.
They include floor-area information.
They include certificate counts.
They include regional breakdowns.

CO2 fields are certificate-derived, not parcel sensors.

packages.title: Part L new-dwelling characteristics QA
facts: MHCLG publishes new-dwelling efficiency characteristics.

The dataset includes property type.
The dataset includes heating-system type.
The dataset includes heat-pump characteristics.
The dataset includes solar-PV characteristics.

packages.title: Building-to-parcel composite binding guard
facts: EPC ratings are estimates from building characteristics.
EPC live tables do not supply parcel boundaries.

Local GHG statistics are broader than parcels.
